Building the application-specific FFmpeg tools

The source ZIP contains the exact FFmpeg, x264 and zlib source archives,
their SHA-256 identities, license notices, configure results, and build scripts.
No upstream source patches are applied. Build selection is in
Build-MinimalFFmpeg.sh. Generated configuration headers are for audit; configure
regenerates them for your build location.

To rebuild from the application repository:
1. Obtain w64devkit x64 2.11.0 and NASM win64 2.16.03 using the URLs and
   SHA-256 hashes in build-manifest.json. Extract both portable toolchains.
   Supply Bash from Git for Windows for x264's configure script.
2. Run tools/Build-MinimalFFmpeg.ps1 -ToolchainDirectory <w64devkit folder>
   -NasmDirectory <folder containing nasm.exe> -BashPath <bash.exe>.
   Portable toolchains require no system installation.
3. The script verifies and extracts deps/FFmpeg/source archives, compiles
   static libraries and the two executables, then checks the feature contract.
   Binaries are under artifacts/media-build/prefix/bin.
4. Run export regression tests before replacing deps/FFmpeg/bin binaries.

To rebuild from just the companion source ZIP:
1. Make an empty working folder containing tools/ and deps/FFmpeg/.
2. Extract the complete ZIP under deps/FFmpeg/.
3. Copy Build-MinimalFFmpeg.ps1, Build-MinimalFFmpeg.sh and
   Test-MinimalFFmpeg.ps1 from that folder to tools/.
4. Follow steps 1–3 above. Windows tar.exe and PowerShell are used to extract
   archives; the compiler and other Unix build utilities are portable.

Media build inputs are source archives, not prebuilt third-party codec DLLs.
GCC's standard Windows libraries are statically linked where applicable;
only Windows system DLLs are imported by the resulting executables.
